Core concept

What is a molecule?

A molecule is made up of two or more atoms that are chemically combined.

Learn
  • An atom can combine with one or more atoms of the same element or different elements to form molecules.Atoms rarely sit alone. They lock together in small groups, and each group is a molecule.
  • A molecule is made up of two or more atoms that are chemically combined.Two is the smallest a molecule can be. Chemically combined means properly locked together, not simply sitting next to each other.
  • Atoms of the same element can combine to form a molecule. For example, a hydrogen molecule is made up of two hydrogen atoms.Both halves are the same kind of atom, so nothing new has been made. It is still the element hydrogen.
  • Atoms of different elements can also combine to form a molecule. For example, a water molecule is made up of two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom.Two different kinds of atom join, and the result behaves nothing like either of them on its own.
  • The total number of atoms in one hydrogen molecule is two, and the total number of atoms in one water molecule is three.To count the atoms in a molecule, count every circle, whatever colour it is.
Key Facts
  • A molecule is made up of two or more atoms that are chemically combined.
  • An atom is the simplest unit of an element. A molecule is two or more atoms joined.
  • A single circle represents one atom. Two or more circles joined together represent a molecule.
Test

How many atoms in total are there in one ammonia molecule, which is made of one nitrogen atom and three hydrogen atoms?

Core concept

How do we represent atoms and molecules on paper?

A simple way to represent atoms and molecules is by using labelled circles.

Learn
  • To represent an atom of an element, a single circle labelled with the chemical symbol of the element is used.One circle, one atom, and the letters inside tell you which element it is.
  • For example, a hydrogen atom can be represented by one circle labelled with H.
  • A hydrogen molecule can be represented by two circles that are labelled with H and joined together.Joining the circles is the part that matters. It shows the atoms are chemically combined.
  • A water molecule can be represented by two circles labelled with H, and one other circle labelled with O, which are joined together.
  • Circles of different colours and sizes are often used to represent atoms so that we can distinguish between them easily.The colours are a convenience for us. They are not a property of the atom.
  • In fact, atoms do not have any colour. This is one limitation of scientific models, which are simplified representations and are not always real and accurate.A model is a thinking tool. Useful, but never mistake the drawing for the thing itself.
Key Facts
  • A molecule is made up of two or more atoms that are chemically combined.
  • Atoms do not have any colour. Colours and sizes in a model are there to help us tell atoms apart.
  • This is one limitation of scientific models, which are simplified representations and are not always real and accurate.

Hook

One extra atom. How much can that possibly change?

Two bottles. Both hold a clear liquid. Both are built from hydrogen and oxygen and nothing else.

Commit to an answer before you read on

Hydrogen peroxide has exactly one more oxygen atom in each molecule than water does. What does that one atom change?

So what is a chemical formula for?

H2O and H2O2 are not descriptions. They are instructions, precise enough that a chemist in another country reads exactly the same molecule you did. Two hydrogen atoms and one oxygen atom. Not roughly. Exactly. The next slide is about how to read one.

📓Now complete your notes: Section C: The chemical formulaWrite the section title, and copy the two formulae H2O and H2O2 with their models.
Core concept

What is a chemical formula?

The chemical formula identifies each element in a molecule by its symbol, and gives the number of atoms of that element.

Learn
  • The chemical formula is another way to represent molecules.Drawing circles is slow. A formula says the same thing in a few characters.
  • It identifies each constituent element in a molecule by its chemical symbol, and indicates the number of atoms of the element.The letters tell you which elements are in it. The small number tells you how many atoms of the element just before it.
  • The chemical formula of hydrogen is H2: one hydrogen molecule contains 2 hydrogen atoms.
  • The chemical formula of water is H2O: one water molecule contains 2 hydrogen atoms and 1 oxygen atom.Where no small number is written, there is exactly one atom of that element. The lone O means one oxygen atom.
Key Facts
  • The chemical formula identifies each constituent element in a molecule by its chemical symbol, and indicates the number of atoms of the element.
  • A symbol written with no small number after it means one atom of that element.
Test

The formula of ammonia is NH3. What does it tell you?

Worked example · the anatomy of a formula
How that answer was reached, step by step
  1. Find the capital letters. Each one starts a chemical symbol: C, H, O. So three different elements are present.
  2. Read the small number after each symbol. It counts the atoms of that symbol only. C6 is six carbon atoms.
  3. Do the same for the rest: H12 is twelve hydrogen atoms, O6 is six oxygen atoms.
  4. Add them up for the total number of atoms: 6 + 12 + 6 = 24.
  5. Count the types of atom, not the number: three types, so glucose is a compound.
One glucose molecule: 24 atoms, 3 types of atom, a molecule of a compound.
Now you fill the gaps. Ethanol has the formula C2H6O. Step 1: the capital letters are C, H and O, so ___ types of atom. Step 2: ___ carbon atoms. Step 3: ___ hydrogen atoms and ___ oxygen atom — a symbol with no small number after it means one. Step 4: the total is 2 + 6 + 1 = ___ atoms. Step 5: ___ types of atom, so ethanol is a ___. Say all five answers out loud, then tap the card below to check them.

Core concept

What is the difference between a molecule of an element and a molecule of a compound?

Count the types of atom. One type makes it an element, more than one makes it a compound.

Before the definitions · commit to an answer

Oxygen, O2, is the gas you are breathing right now. Ozone, O3, is the gas high in the atmosphere that blocks ultraviolet light — and breathing it would burn your lungs. Two different substances that behave nothing alike. Yet every single atom in both of them is an oxygen atom. Is ozone a molecule of an element or a molecule of a compound?

Learn
  • A molecule of an element consists of only one type of atoms that are chemically combined.Everything in the molecule is the same kind of atom, so the substance is still just that element.
  • Examples are nitrogen, written as N with a small 2, and oxygen, written as O with a small 2.
  • A molecule of a compound consists of two or more types of atoms that are chemically combined.As soon as a second kind of atom joins in, you have a compound, and it behaves like neither of the elements that built it.
  • An example is nitrogen dioxide, which is written as N followed by O with a small 2.One nitrogen atom and two oxygen atoms. Two types of atom, so it is a compound.
  • Hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, chlorine and iodine are all elements whose molecules hold two atoms of the same type.
  • Water, ammonia, carbon monoxide, carbon dioxide and hydrogen chloride are all compounds.Read the formula of any of them and you will find more than one capital letter, which is the giveaway. Cl₂ has two letters but only one capital, so it is a molecule of an element, not a compound.
Key Facts
  • A molecule of an element consists of only one type of atoms that are chemically combined.
  • A molecule of a compound consists of two or more types of atoms that are chemically combined.
  • Count the types of atom, not the number of atoms. A hydrogen molecule has two atoms but only one type.

Chemically combined, or just sitting in the same jar?

Two jars. Both contain hydrogen atoms and oxygen atoms. Only one of them contains a compound, and the difference is the two words the examiner is looking for.

Watch out

Two words carry the marks in both definitions: chemically combined. “Stuck together”, “touching” and “mixed” all describe jar 1, and none of them will be given the mark. Jar 1 is a mixture: hydrogen molecules and oxygen molecules together in one space, but not chemically combined. Jar 2 is a compound.

How do chemists build a molecule that has never existed?

Some molecules are formed from the combination of many atoms, and for a long time nobody could build them in a laboratory.

Science at work: the molecular gastronomist

Molecular gastronomy involves the study of molecules in the physical and chemical processes that occur in food during cooking. Some chefs prepare dishes that have new types of tastes, textures or appearances by applying scientific principles and techniques of preparing food.

Brain dump · 60 seconds

Close everything else. Write down everything you can remember about molecules and chemical formulae. Words, formulae, drawings in words — anything. Do not look back through the slides.

Tick off everything you got. Anything you missed is what to revise tonight.
  • A molecule is two or more atoms that are chemically combined.
  • An atom can combine with atoms of the same element, or of different elements.
  • One labelled circle is one atom; joined circles are a molecule.
  • Atoms have no colour; the colours in a model are ours, which is a limitation of models.
  • A chemical formula gives each element by its symbol and the number of atoms of that element.
  • A symbol with no small number after it means one atom.
  • A molecule of an element has only one type of atom, chemically combined.
  • A molecule of a compound has two or more types of atom, chemically combined.
  • Count types of atom, not the number of atoms: S8 has eight atoms and is still an element.
  • Chemists can plan and build new molecules: Woodward’s team made cholesterol, chlorophyll and vitamin B12.
